summary_paraphrase: Proverbs 1:7 says wisdom begins with the fear of the LORD. Verses 10–19 describe men who chase a quick gain together and get caught by it.
challenge: Name one shortcut you've been tempted by this month. Decide today that you won't take it.

summary_paraphrase: Proverbs 2:4 tells you to search for understanding the way you would search for silver or buried treasure.
challenge: Give ten minutes to one question about God or life that you usually skip past.

summary_paraphrase: Proverbs 3:5–6: trust the LORD with all your heart and don't lean on your own understanding. Verse 9: honor Him with your firstfruits.
challenge: Before your first decision today, pray one sentence over it.

summary_paraphrase: Proverbs 4:23: guard your heart above all else, because everything you do flows from it.
challenge: Take one input out of your day (an app, a feed, a show) and notice what changes.

summary_paraphrase: Proverbs 5:15–18 warns against straying and calls a man to delight in the wife of his youth.
challenge: Do one specific, unasked kindness for your wife or the person closest to you.

summary_paraphrase: Proverbs 6:6–8 holds up the ant, which works without a boss. Verses 16–19 list seven things the LORD hates.
challenge: Finish the one task you've been putting off longest. Today.

summary_paraphrase: Proverbs 7 traces a young man drifting step by step into a trap he could have walked around.
challenge: Find the first step of a habit you want to quit and take that step out.

summary_paraphrase: In Proverbs 8, wisdom stands at the gates and the crossroads, calling out to anyone who will listen.
challenge: Ask an older man you respect one real question this week.

summary_paraphrase: Proverbs 9:8–9: correct a wise man and he will love you for it.
challenge: Ask someone, "What's one thing I could do better?" Then just say thank you.

summary_paraphrase: Proverbs 10:9: whoever walks in integrity walks securely. Verse 4: diligent hands bring wealth.
challenge: Fix one small thing you've been fudging, like a number, an excuse or a promise.

summary_paraphrase: Proverbs 11:2: when pride comes, disgrace follows, but humility brings wisdom. Verse 25: the generous are refreshed.
challenge: Give something away today without telling anyone.

summary_paraphrase: Proverbs 12:1 is blunt: whoever loves discipline loves knowledge. Verse 25: anxiety weighs a man down, and a kind word cheers him up.
challenge: Send one encouraging message to a man who's carrying a lot.

summary_paraphrase: Proverbs 13:20: walk with the wise and become wise. A companion of fools suffers harm.
challenge: Look at the five people you spend the most time with. Make one call that moves you toward the wise.

summary_paraphrase: Proverbs 14:12: there is a way that seems right to a man, but its end is the way to death.
challenge: Write down a choice you've justified to yourself. Read it out loud. Does it hold up?

summary_paraphrase: Proverbs 15:1: a gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
challenge: In your next tense conversation, lower your voice and slow down on purpose.

summary_paraphrase: Proverbs 16:3: commit your work to the LORD and your plans will be established. Verse 18: pride goes before destruction.
challenge: Pray over your to-do list before you start it.

summary_paraphrase: Proverbs 17:17: a friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity. Verse 22: a cheerful heart is good medicine.
challenge: Check on a friend you haven't heard from in a while.

summary_paraphrase: Proverbs 18:13: answering before you've listened is folly and shame. Verse 10: the name of the LORD is a strong tower.
challenge: In every conversation today, let the other person finish before you answer.

summary_paraphrase: Proverbs 19:11: good sense makes a man slow to anger, and it is his glory to overlook an offense.
challenge: Let one offense go today without bringing it up.

summary_paraphrase: Proverbs 20:6: many men claim to be loyal, but a faithful man, who can find?
challenge: Keep one promise you made that everyone else has forgotten.

summary_paraphrase: Proverbs 21:3: doing what is right and just matters more to the LORD than sacrifice.
challenge: Make right one thing that's been unfair, even if it costs you.

summary_paraphrase: Proverbs 22:1: a good name is worth more than great riches. Verse 6: train up a child in the way he should go.
challenge: Spend fifteen minutes of undivided time with a kid in your life.

summary_paraphrase: Proverbs 23:4–5: don't wear yourself out to get rich. Money can sprout wings and fly away.
challenge: Ask whether one purchase you're planning is about need or about status.

summary_paraphrase: Proverbs 24:16: the righteous falls seven times and rises again. Verse 10: if you faint in the day of adversity, your strength is small.
challenge: Get back on the habit you dropped. Don't wait for Monday.

summary_paraphrase: Proverbs 25:28: a man without self-control is like a city whose walls are broken down.
challenge: Pick one appetite to say no to today, just once, on purpose.

summary_paraphrase: Proverbs 26:11: like a dog returning to its vomit, a fool repeats his folly. Verses 4–5: know when to answer and when not to.
challenge: Delete or block the thing you keep going back to.

summary_paraphrase: Proverbs 27:17: as iron sharpens iron, one man sharpens another. Verse 1: don't boast about tomorrow.
challenge: Invite one man to meet up regularly, for coffee, a walk or a workout.

summary_paraphrase: Proverbs 28:13: whoever hides his sins won't prosper, but whoever confesses and turns from them finds mercy.
challenge: Tell God plainly what you've been hiding. Then tell one trusted man.

summary_paraphrase: Proverbs 29:25: the fear of man lays a snare, but whoever trusts in the LORD is safe.
challenge: Do one right thing today that you've avoided because of what people might think.

summary_paraphrase: Proverbs 30:8–9 prays for neither poverty nor riches, only daily bread, so that you don't forget God or dishonor Him.
challenge: Thank God out loud for three ordinary things you have today.

summary_paraphrase: Proverbs 31:8–9: open your mouth for those who can't speak for themselves. Verses 10–31 honor a woman of strength.
challenge: Use your voice once today for someone who has less of one.
